solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Support for basic form of lighting

definitions.text: Support for basic form of lighting

parts.words: Support for basic form of lighting
parts.note: read plainly, a holder that props up the simple wax light used before gas and electricity

explanation.surface: Someone describes the foundation of an elementary lighting system.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder made to keep a wax taper upright is exactly the support for the most basic light source.

clue.text: Host has upset distingusihed painter? Gosh!

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters for the painter upside down, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is a painter elected to the Royal Academy (misspelt as printed)
my! is an exclamation of surprise like gosh!

explanation.surface: A host has offended an eminent artist, to the onlooker's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns RA into AR. RA (Royal Academician) is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, a British honour for distinguished painters.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a great multitude, especially an armed force, as in the heavenly host.

clue.text: Dope beginning to dance on mat

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so take only the opening letter of dance

parts.note: a rug is a small floor mat

explanation.surface: Someone takes narcotics and then starts dancing on a mat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes D from 'dance'; 'on' places it above RUG in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for a narcotic, the same thing as an illegal substance taken for its effect.

clue.text: More futile row begun by English politician

indicators.note: the word for row comes after, so it is begun by the other pieces

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A political row grows more pointless once an English MP starts it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'begun by' means the row word is the end of the answer, with the other pieces in front; 'More futile' is the comparative definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptier means more hollow and meaningless, a comparative synonym for more futile.

clue.text: Left-winger's progress at steady pace

definitions.meaning: short for a Trotskyist, a hard-left activist
to move at a gait between walking and running, as a horse does

explanation.surface: A socialist moves steadily forward.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for a follower of Trotsky and the name of a jogging gait.

clue.text: Gosh, fixed around front of leg, there's a piece of armour!

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh!

indicators.note: the word for fixed goes around the letter taken from leg

parts.note: set means fixed, firm

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, here of leg

explanation.surface: An onlooker is amazed to find armour strapped round a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' takes the first letter of 'leg'; 'around' wraps the word for fixed round it. Cor! is a British exclamation like gosh!
explanation.definitionFit: A corslet is a piece of body armour covering the trunk.

clue.text: Where one may find mite in hot water?

definitions.text: Where one may find mite in hot water?

parts.words: Where one may find mite in hot water?
parts.note: a tiny mite lives on a rug, while the idiom for someone summoned for a telling-off means being in trouble

explanation.surface: A question about where a small bug might be found in scalding water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot water' is not a liquid but trouble: being reprimanded by the boss, while a dust mite literally lives on the floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being reprimanded, in trouble, which is what in hot water also means.

clue.text: Lad compares various old animals

indicators.note: various signals the letters of these words are arranged in a different order

explanation.surface: A boy makes comparisons between different things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges LADCOMPARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelopard is an archaic name for the giraffe, from camel plus leopard.

clue.text: Old emperor's home with Manx cat!

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word cat loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its tail

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler keeps a tailless cat at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' cuts T from CAT, as a Manx cat (from the Isle of Man) is tailless; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca was the emperor of the old Peruvian empire.

clue.text: Our ma getting upset, needing support in respect of self-esteem

indicators.note: upset means the letters of these words are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a prop is a support
re means concerning, in respect of

explanation.surface: Mother is upset and needs reassurance about her pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' turns OURMA into AMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means self-love, a borrowed term for self-esteem.

clue.text: Mark will go around hospital for you as before

indicators.note: the word for mark is placed around the hospital abbreviation

parts.note: a tee is the mark aimed at in curling or quoits

explanation.surface: A sign will be put round a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will go around' puts TEE round H.
explanation.definitionFit: The old objective form of thou is the archaic word for you.

clue.text: Flag opening, vast when unfurled

indicators.note: unfurled suggests something spread out and rearranged, signalling a new order of the letters

explanation.surface: A huge flag is spread out at a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when unfurled' rearranges OPENINGVAST; 'Flag' looks like a banner but is a flagstone.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag is a flat slab of stone used for paving.

clue.text: Ms West in a spin bumping into walker with crushing force

indicators.note: the reversed name is pushed inside the word for walker

parts.note: a stroller is one who walks leisurely

indicators.note: spinning round turns the name so it reads backwards

parts.note: Mae West was the American film actress

explanation.surface: The actress spins and collides with a walker with great force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a spin' turns the actress's name backwards; 'bumping into' pushes it inside the walker. Mae West was a 1930s Hollywood star.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is used attributively for overwhelming force, as in steamroller tactics; the noun is an overpowering force.

clue.text: Star 'urries following worker

indicators.note: the word for hurries comes after the word for worker

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
hurries with its H dropped gives hares with its H dropped too

explanation.surface: A celebrity scurries along after a labourer, in Cockney speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'urries is hurries without its H, so the synonym hares loses its H too, giving ARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is a red supergiant, the brightest star in Scorpius.

clue.text: Salvationists gathered around tree in US town

indicators.note: the Salvationists' letters surround the tree

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army
an elm is a tree

explanation.surface: Salvation Army members cluster round a tree in an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered around' means the Salvationists surround the tree. Selma, Alabama, is known for the 1965 civil rights marches.
explanation.definitionFit: Selma is a city in Alabama, famous for the 1965 civil rights marches.

clue.text: English with many possessions taken in by little woman in Middle Eastern town

indicators.note: the pieces are taken inside the little woman's name

parts.note: Jo March is one of the Little Women in Alcott's novel
rich means having many possessions

explanation.surface: A wealthy Englishman is housed by a small woman in a desert town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' puts English and rich inside the little woman: Jo, from Louisa May Alcott's Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Jericho is a town in the West Bank, in the Middle East.

clue.text: Obscure fellow descending on a biblical land

indicators.note: in a down clue the fellow's name comes down on top of the following letter

parts.note: Jude the Obscure is Thomas Hardy's novel

explanation.surface: A shady character comes down on a holy land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descending on' places JUDE above A.
explanation.definitionFit: Judea is the southern region of ancient Palestine named in the Bible.

clue.text: Deny destroying brute

indicators.note: destroying the word breaks its letters up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone denies wrecking a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying' rearranges BRUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut a claim is to refute or deny it.

clue.text: A queen, originally one to run country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one; originally says it stands at the start of the answer
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A queen was first chosen to rule a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' (at first) says that one and run come before A and queen; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a Middle Eastern country.

clue.text: Region's stadium lacking name

indicators.note: lacking means one letter is missing from the stadium word

parts.note: an arena is a stadium

explanation.surface: A district's sports ground has no name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes N from ARENA; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district.

clue.text: Colour of a gong, right?

parts.note: gong is slang for a medal or honour such as the MBE

explanation.surface: A question about the colour of a gong.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal; the MBE is an order of chivalry awarded in the honours list.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a yellowish-orange colour.

clue.text: Everyone, for instance, runs round quickly

parts.note: all means everyone
eg is short for exempli gratia, for example
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Everybody, for example, jogs a lap quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a musical direction meaning briskly or fast.

clue.text: One set of holy books held by group on the rampage

indicators.note: the pieces are held inside the word for group

parts.note: a ring is a group or gang
I is the Roman numeral one
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A gang holds a religious text while rampaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts one and the holy books inside the group; 'on the rampage' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioting describes a mob running wild, on the rampage.

clue.text: Animal in stream in Indian territory

indicators.note: the stream word sits in the territory name

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: An animal is found in a stream in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the stream inside the Indian territory; 'Animal' is the definition at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The gorilla is the largest ape, an animal.

clue.text: Help to protect bird, not a sensible type

indicators.note: the help word surrounds and so protects the bird

parts.note: aid means help
the rhea is a flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Someone helps shelter a bird, though not wisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' means the help word wraps round the bird; the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is a stupid, empty-headed person.

clue.text: Loss of part of allotment to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left
part of signals a run of letters taken from inside allotment

explanation.surface: Losing a share of a garden plot to the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' gives LLOT from 'allotment'; 'to the west' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll is a cost or loss, as in the death toll.

clue.text: Stud man who has others working for him?

definitions.meaning: a raised knob or ornamental stud on a surface

definitions.text: man who has others working for him?

explanation.surface: A ladies' man who employs others.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is both a raised ornamental knob and the person in charge.

clue.text: Post set up for Irishman

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up turns the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: mail is post

explanation.surface: Letters are put up for an Irish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns MAIL to LIAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Liam is a common Irish man's name.

clue.text: Flowing water and what it can't do

definitions.meaning: a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: Running water and its inability to catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: A burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a small stream and to be on fire, which water never does.

clue.text: 'Disgraceful unionism!' — I go mad

indicators.note: mad signals the letters are scrambled crazily

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy at disgraceful trade unionism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges UNIONISM and IGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignominious means shameful, causing public disgrace.

clue.text: No sort of railway? Often that's so at that time!

definitions.text: Often that's so at that time

parts.note: taken as written
an el is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A question about railways and the season when they stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to the wordplay: at Christmas there is often no railway running, so the festive season is the time it is so.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas, the festive season, is when trains often do not run.

clue.text: Agreement to smuggle in gin that's ill-gotten shipload

indicators.note: the agreement word takes the other letters secretly inside it

parts.note: consent is agreement

indicators.note: something ill-gotten is wrongly come by, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the gin letters plus M for money, which the printed clue omits

explanation.surface: A shipment of smuggled gin is obtained illegally under an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-gotten' rearranges the gin letters and 'to smuggle in' puts them inside the agreement word; the printed clue omits the M needed for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A consignment is a batch of goods shipped, a shipload.
